displayPattern: Amber status LED on a Carrier 59SC5 stays on, with no flashes
meaning: Control has 24 VAC power: a steady amber LED is not a fault code.
causes: The furnace control has 24 VAC power and is not flashing a status code
diySteps: A steady amber light matches the label's continuous-on line. It means the control has 24 VAC. It does not name a failed part
If the furnace still has no heat, watch for a flash code and look that number up. A technician is the next step when there is no heat and the light never flashes a code
proAdvice: Call a licensed HVAC technician if there is no heat and the LED stays on without a flash code. Continuous on is the powered, no-code state. Rapid flashing is reversed polarity, which is a different pattern.
safetyNote: If you smell gas, do not touch any electrical switch or use a phone in the building; leave immediately and call your gas supplier from outside. Turn off electrical power at the furnace switch or breaker before opening any panel, and never bypass or jumper a limit, rollout or pressure switch. Gas valve, burner, venting, wiring and control-board work should be done by a licensed HVAC technician.
sourceTitle: Carrier 59SC5A installation, start-up, operating and service instructions (Catalog No. 59SC5A-01SI), Fig. 55 service label. Read 2026-11-07
